newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent higher in light, featureless tradeE.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent higher in light, featureless tradeE.

text.p: IPE Brent futures were moderately higher on Monday in a quiet and relatively news barren market, brokers said.
"It could get a bit choppy later on with the Jan expiry coming up," one trader said. "There isn't really any fresh news out there, we're just seeing a bit of a play of the spreads."

January Brent, which expires at the close of Monday's session was trading seven cents higher at 1103 GMT, having ended $1.01 up on Friday. February Brent was trading 21 cents higher. January gas oil was up $4.50 at $218.25. "The gas oil's been helped up by the cold weather forecasts," said another trader.

Independent forecaster, Weather Services Corporation (WSC) said a blast of cold weather could hit the key heating oil market of the northeast United States by the weekend, but in the meantime they forecast below normal heating needs in the region.

In Europe, WSC forecast above normal temperatures in northwest Europe for a period extending into the next 10 days, but in northeast Europe temperatures were seen below normal into the next five days.
Traders said the market was paying limited attention to postering by Iran's leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei that the United States was preparing an attack on Iran.

Khamenei told Revolutionary Guards on Saturday that U.S. media allegations over Tehran's alleged involvement in the bomb which killed 19 U.S. airmen at a Saudi base in June would be used as premise for a military attack on his country.
"We're not taking this too seriously," said one trader. "The whole story is based on newspaper allegations which came out last week," said the trader.

"Iran's Ayatollah suggests that a U.S. attack is imminent but his statement was probably exaggerated for the consumption of the military personel he was addressing at the time," said commodity broker GNI's Leslie Nicholas in his daily report.
Loading of the first tanker of Iraqi oil was reported to be nearing completion, officials at the Turkish port of Ceyhan -- terminus of a twin pipeline from Iraqi Kirkuk -- said early on Monday.
They said that the Gole tanker had loaded 153,500 tonnes of Kirkuk crude which will be used by Turkey's state refiner Tupras.
